To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the aggregation of ferroparticles in chains in a dilute ferroliquid is enhanced in an applied magnetic field.

the theory of aggregation in flexible chains in ferrofluids has been generalized to the case when the interparticle magnetic interaction between neighboring ferroparticles is taken into account and that the field dependent chain orientational correlations result in the field-dependent chain lengthening and higher magnetization of aggregated ferrofluids in comparison with the case of Langevin ferrofluids.

(1) the chain partition function in the case of an arbitrary magnetic field is expressed in terms of the rotation matrix; (2) the internal chain correlations are responsible for the field-dependent chain lengthening; (3) the field-dependent chain partition function and the magnetization are calculated; (4) the magnetization is higher in comparison with the case of uncorrelated chains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the theoretical description of the magnetic behavior of ferrofluids in the vicinity of a phase transition to the state of chain aggregation under the influence of an external magnetic field.
the aggregation of magnetic particles in chains under the action of a magnetic field and the formation of a chain structure in the ferrofluid.
the theory of the chain formation and magnetization in ferrofluids under an arbitrarily strong magnetic field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ferrofluid aggregation in chains and the field dependent magnetization of the aggregates are the most important factors which determine the magnetization of ferrofluids in the low field range.

the aggregation of ferrofluid particles in flexible chains in a magnetic field results in the field dependent increase of the initial susceptibility, the magnetization, and the coercivity of ferrofluid.
the theory presented in this work is able to describe quantitatively the magnetic properties of aggregated ferrofluids in a wide range of the magnetic field and particle concentration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the theory of particle aggregation in flexible chains in ferrofluids has been extended to the case of a magnetic field of any strength.

in the case of a sufficiently high magnetic field, the chain lengthening and the field dependent orientational correlations lead to the increase in the initial susceptibility and the decrease in the saturation magnetization of the ferrofluid.
the theory of particle association is a powerful instrument for the investigation of ferrofluid aggregation in chains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the field dependent chain distribution is not described by the Langevin function.
the chain distribution and magnetization of the diluted ferrofluids are strongly affected by the magnetic field and the interparticle interaction.
the field dependent chain partition function is the main factor responsible for the magnetization enhancement in the aggregated ferrocolloidal ferrofluids.
